bottom_arrow: The first paragraph defines Phi^k:Ghat^t(K)→K by f↦(-1)^(k-1)[t^(k-1)](f-prime/f). Hence the lower-right object is its domain and the lower-left K its codomain. More explicitly,the upper/right route sends1+Xt to lambda_u(1+Xt) and then to(1+Xt)^(circle k-prime)=1+X^(k-prime)t. Applying Phi^k gives X^(kk-prime),which is the value of the left vertical Phi^(kk-prime) on1+Xt. This is exactly the two displayed calculations immediately below the square,and fixes the lower arrow right-to-left without changing any object or label.
coefficient_parenthesis: The page first defines Phi^k(f)=(-1)^(k-1)[t^(k-1)](f-prime/f). For f=1+Xt,formal differentiation gives f-prime/f=X/(1+Xt)=sum_(j>=0)(-1)^j X^(j+1)t^j. Its(k-1)-st coefficient is(-1)^(k-1)X^k. Multiplication by the sign from the definition gives X^k. Equivalently,the coefficient of t^(k-1) in(-1)^(k-1)X/(1+Xt) is exactly X^k,so inserting that factor inside the parenthetical coefficient-series repairs only the omitted sign. The denominator parentheses group the same formal inverse;the source solidus is retained. At k=2 in Z[X],the unsigned source coefficient is-X^2,whereas Phi^2(1+Xt)=X^2. No coefficient number or exponent is changed.
